title: The Dignity of Being Seen: Loving People Who Are Sick
subject: Compassionate presence and whole-person care for people living with serious illness
angle: Explore how love protects dignity by seeing a person rather than a diagnosis, listening without trying to fix everything, and remaining present through suffering.

title: More Than a Need: Loving Our Neighbors in Poverty
subject: Human dignity, poverty, and solidarity
angle: Challenge language and actions that reduce people to their needs, and show how solidarity, listening, and shared agency express love without paternalism.

title: Welcome at the Margins: Loving People Society Ostracizes
subject: Belonging, social exclusion, and the dignity of ostracized people
angle: Examine the everyday choices that create belonging for people who are stigmatized, isolated, or pushed outside community life.

title: When Politics Makes Strangers of Neighbors
subject: Political polarization and the discipline of loving across disagreement
angle: Explore how political identity can turn disagreement into contempt, and offer practices for truthful, principled conversation that refuses dehumanization.

title: Faith Without Fear: Loving Across Religious Differences
subject: Religious difference, pluralism, and cooperation
angle: Show how people can remain rooted in their own convictions while building trust, protecting religious dignity, and working alongside neighbors of other faiths or no faith.

title: Beyond the Lines We Inherit: Race, Memory, and Neighborly Love
subject: Racial division, honest memory, and nonviolent reconciliation
angle: Consider why love requires truth about racial injustice, respect for lived experience, and nonviolent commitment to repair rather than denial or blame.

title: Building Together: The Carter Work Project and the Practice of Unity
subject: People from different backgrounds building homes together through the Carter Work Project
angle: Use a documented community-building effort to show how shared work can turn concern into relationship and unite people across social and economic differences.

title: Cooperation Across Faiths: Interfaith America in Practice
subject: People of different religious and nonreligious backgrounds cooperating for the common good
angle: Center real examples of bridge-building and shared action while respecting the distinct beliefs and identities participants bring.

title: From Political Opponents to Civic Partners
subject: Cross-partisan citizens building relationships and serving their communities together
angle: Focus on real-world practices that help people move from political suspicion to shared civic responsibility without erasing meaningful disagreement.
